     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
     5	
     6	## Employment Status
     7	
     8	84% of the 65,437 respondents are currently working (full-time, part-time, or freelancing). Full-time employment is the dominant mode at 69%, followed by independent contracting/freelancing at 16.4% and full-time students at 13.2%.
     9	
    10	In the United States specifically, full-time employment dropped from 69% in 2023 to 64.8% in 2024. In the U.K. and Ukraine, non-full-time respondents lean toward independent contracting, while in Germany and India they are more likely to be full-time students.
    11	
    12	## Work Environment Trends
    13	
    14	Hybrid work remains the most common arrangement at 42%, consistent with 2023. Remote work accounts for 38%. In-person work has risen for the third consecutive year — from 15% in 2022 to 16% in 2023 to 20% in 2024 — signaling a gradual return-to-office trend.
    15	
    16	## Company Size
    17	
    18	47% of respondents work for organizations with fewer than 100 employees. The distribution across 42,827 respondents:
    19	
    20	| Company Size | Share |
    21	|---|---|
    22	| Freelancer / solo | 6.1% |
    23	| 2–9 employees | 10.4% |
    24	| 10–19 employees | 8.9% |
    25	| 20–99 employees | 21.2% |
    26	| 100–499 employees | 18.5% |
    27	| 500–999 employees | 6.7% |
    28	| 1,000–4,999 employees | 11.0% |
    29	| 5,000–9,999 employees | 3.8% |
    30	| 10,000+ employees | 11.4% |
    31	
    32	## Salary by Developer Type
    33	
    34	Median annual compensation (USD, all respondents) varies dramatically by role. The top and bottom roles are shown below (22,677 salary responses, 34.7% response rate):
    35	
    36	| Developer Type | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    37	|---|---|---|
    38	| Senior Executive | $127,388 | ~17 |
    39	| Dev Advocate | $124,203 | ~16 |
    40	| Manager | $115,999 | ~15 |
    41	| Dev Experience | $109,483 | ~12 |
    42	| SRE | $99,099 | ~10 |
    43	| Cloud Infra. Engineer | $96,666 | ~13 |
    44	| Blockchain | $85,925 | ~9 |
    45	| Product Manager | $80,000 | ~14 |
    46	| Full-stack | $63,333 | ~10 |
    47	| Front-end | $48,787 | ~8 |
    48	| Student | $15,466 | ~2 |
    49	
    50	Site reliability engineers and cloud infrastructure engineers are the highest-paid purely technical roles, reflecting their critical importance in keeping digital services running. Regionally, mobile developers earn more in the U.S., data engineers top the charts in Germany and Ukraine, and back-end developers lead in India and the U.K.
    51	
    52	![Salary by developer type — bar chart](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    53	
    54	![Salary vs. experience by developer type — scatter plot](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    55	
    56	## Salary by Programming Language
    57	
    58	Developers using niche functional languages earn the most. The overall reported salary range has dropped roughly $10K compared to 2023, now averaging $60–75K USD vs. $70–85K USD last year.
    59	
    60	| Language | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| Erlang | ~$97,000 | ~12 |
    63	| Clojure | ~$95,000 | ~11 |
    64	| Elixir | ~$93,000 | ~11 |
    65	| Perl | ~$90,000 | ~19 |
    66	| Ruby | ~$89,000 | ~11 |
    67	| Scala | ~$88,000 | ~9 |
    68	| Go | ~$76,000 | ~9 |
    69	| Python | ~$67,000 | ~9 |
    70	| JavaScript | ~$64,000 | ~10 |
    71	| PHP | ~$49,000 | ~10 |
    72	| Dart | ~$44,000 | ~8 |
    73	| Prolog | ~$43,000 | ~9 |
    74	
    75	![Salary vs. experience by language — scatter plot](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    76	
    77	## Technology Purchasing Influence
    78	
    79	62% of respondents have influence over technology purchases at their organizations. Senior executives (99%), engineering managers (87%), and product managers (77%) wield the most influence. 60% of respondents prefer a build-and-buy approach over purely building or buying. Starting a free trial (75%) and asking other developers (73%) are the top methods for evaluating new tools.
    80	
    81	## Key Findings
    82	
    83	- **Full-time employment is softening**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 percentage points year-over-year; freelancing and contracting remain significant at 16%+.
    84	- **In-person work is creeping back**: now at 20%, up from 15% in 2022, though hybrid (42%) still dominates.
    85	- **DevRel and leadership roles command premium pay**: Senior Executives ($127K), Dev Advocates ($124K), and Managers ($116K) top the salary chart, all with 15+ years average experience.
    86	- **Niche functional languages correlate with higher pay**: Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir developers earn >$93K median, while mainstream languages like JavaScript and PHP sit well below $65K.
    87	- **Developers are key purchase influencers**: with 62% having a say in tech buying decisions, vendor strategies should target individual contributors, not just management.

    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.
    13	
    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`
    15	
    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically
    23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. (Note: the Eight Confirmations in Step 4 are ⛔ BLOCKING — the AI should present recommendations and seek user confirmation when possible. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN
    27	> 7. **SEQUENTIAL PAGE GENERATION ONLY** — In Executor Step 6, after the global design context is confirmed, SVG pages MUST be generated sequentially page by page in one continuous pass. Grouped page batches (for example, 5 pages at a time) are FORBIDDEN
    28	
    29	> [!IMPORTANT]
    30	> ## 🌐 Language & Communication Rule
    31	>
    32	> - **Response language**: Always match the language of the user's input and provided source materials. For example, if the user asks in Chinese, respond in Chinese; if the source material is in English, respond in English.
    33	> - **Explicit override**: If the user explicitly requests a specific language (e.g., "请用英文回答" or "Reply in Chinese"), use that language instead.
    34	> - **Template format**: The `design_spec.md` file MUST always follow its original English template structure (section headings, field names), regardless of the conversation language. Content values within the template may be in the user's language.

   128	
   129	Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:

   131	```xml

   137	### Key Takeaway Box
   138	
   139	Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:
   140	
   141	```
   142	Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50

   148	
   149	## Speaker Notes Style
   150	
   151	### Narrative Tone
   152	
   153	Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.
   154	
   155	### Stage Direction Markers
   156	
   157	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   158	|--------|---------|---------|
   159	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
   160	| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
   161	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |
   162	
   163	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   164	
   165	- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
   166	- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
   167	- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
   168	- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
   169	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`
   170	
   171	### Notes Example
   172	
   173	```markdown
   174	# 03_key_findings
   175	
   176	[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.
   177	
   178	First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
   179	[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]
   180	
   181	Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
   182	Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.
   183	
   184	Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
   185	Duration: 2 minutes
   186	```

     2	
     3	Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
     8	
     9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
    10	
    11	| Banned Feature | Description |
    12	|----------------|-------------|
    13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
    14	| `mask` | Masks |
    15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
    16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
    17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
    18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
    19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
    20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
    21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
    22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
    23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
    24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
    25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
    30	
    31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
    32	|---------------|---------------------|
    33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
    35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
    36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
    37	
    38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
    43	
    44	### Presentations
    45	
    46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
    47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
    48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
    49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
    50	
    51	### Social Media
    52	
    53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
    54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
    55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
    56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
    57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
    58	
    59	### Marketing Materials
    60	
    61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
    62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
    63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
    64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
    65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
    66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
    67	
    68	---
    69	
    70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
    71	
    72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
    73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
    74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
    75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
    76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
    77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
    78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
    79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
    80	
    81	---
    82	
    83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
    84	
    85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
    86	
    87	```bash
    88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
    89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
    90	
    91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
    92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
    93	
    94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
    95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
    96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
    97	```
    98	
    99	**Prohibited**:
   100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
   101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
   102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
   103	
   104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```
   173	
   174	### Image Overlay
   175	
   176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
   177	
   178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
   179	
   180	```xml
   181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
   182	<defs>
   183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
   185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
   186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
   187	  </linearGradient>
   188	</defs>
   189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
   190	```
   191	
   192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
   193	
   194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
   195	
   196	```xml
   197	<defs>
   198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
   199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
   201	  </linearGradient>
   202	</defs>
   203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
   204	```
   205	
   206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
   207	
   208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
   209	
   210	```xml
   211	<defs>
   212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
   213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
   215	  </radialGradient>
   216	</defs>
   217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
   218	```
   219	
   220	#### Brand Color Overlay
   221	
   222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
   223	
   224	```xml
   225	<defs>
   226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
   228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
   229	  </linearGradient>
   230	</defs>
   231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
   232	```

   234	### Quick-Reference Table
   235	
   236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
   237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
   238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
   239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
   240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |

   242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
   243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

# Speaker Notes — Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends

## Slide 1: Cover
Welcome to our analysis of the 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey. This presentation draws on responses from 65,437 developers across 180+ countries, covering employment patterns, work environment preferences, compensation by role and technology, and developer purchasing behavior. The data was collected in early 2024 and published at stackoverflow.co/2024/work.

## Slide 2: 84% of Developers Are Working, but Full-Time Employment Dips in the U.S.
Let's start with employment status. Globally, 84% of respondents are currently working — either full-time, part-time, or as freelancers. Full-time employment represents 69% of the global workforce, while 16.4% work as freelancers or contractors, and 13.2% are full-time students. However, the U.S. shows a notable shift: full-time employment dropped from 69% to 64.8% year-over-year, a 4.2 percentage point decline. This suggests either more developers moving into contracting roles, pursuing further education, or experiencing layoffs. Freelancing holds steady at 16.4% both globally and in the U.S., indicating a durable gig-economy layer. Regional variations exist: the U.K. and Ukraine lean more toward independent contracting, while Germany and India show higher student populations.

## Slide 3: In-Person Work Rises to 20% While Hybrid Holds Steady at 42%
Turning to work environment, hybrid remains the dominant arrangement at 42%, unchanged from 2023. Remote work also holds steady at 38%. The key movement is in-person work, which has risen for three consecutive years: from 15% in 2022, to 16% in 2023, to 20% in 2024. This is a 5 percentage point increase over two years — not a sudden mandate, but a gradual return-to-office trend. For organizations, the implication is clear: plan for a hybrid-first future. The 20% in-person figure is still the minority, and the combined remote-plus-hybrid total of 80% means most developers expect location flexibility.

## Slide 4: Senior Executives Top $127K; Full-Stack Developers Average $63K
Now let's examine compensation by role. Senior Executives lead at $127,388 annually, followed by Developer Advocates at $124,203 and Engineering Managers at $115,999. These top three roles all require 15+ years of experience on average. Moving down the spectrum, we see Site Reliability Engineers at $99,099 and Cloud Infrastructure specialists at $96,666. The gap between leadership and individual contributor roles is significant: Full-Stack Developers average $63,333 and Front-End Developers $48,787 — roughly half to one-third of executive compensation. Developer Experience engineers, a growing specialty, command $109,483, reflecting the strategic importance of developer tooling and platform engineering.

## Slide 5: Salary Climbs with Experience, but Diminishing Returns Appear After 15 Years
This scatter plot shows the relationship between years of professional experience and median annual salary. The trend is clear: compensation rises steeply from 0 to 10 years, then begins to flatten. After approximately 15 years, the curve plateaus, with diminishing returns for each additional year of experience. The orange dashed trend line illustrates this pattern. Notably, senior roles show the widest salary dispersion — experienced developers can earn anywhere from $80K to $130K+ depending on their specialization, company size, and geography. For talent leaders, this means retention strategies for 10+ year veterans must emphasize scope, autonomy, and equity rather than just base salary increases.

## Slide 6: Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir Command the Highest Language Premiums
Language specialization creates significant compensation premiums. Erlang leads at approximately $97,000 median salary, followed by Clojure at ~$95K and Elixir at ~$93K. These are all functional programming languages with relatively small talent pools. On the mainstream side, Go commands ~$76K, Python ~$67K, and JavaScript ~$64K. At the lower end, PHP sits at ~$49K. The gap between niche functional languages and mainstream web stacks is over 50%. This premium reflects supply-demand dynamics: fewer developers know these languages, but the companies that use them — often in fintech, telecom, and distributed systems — are willing to pay for that expertise.

## Slide 7: Nearly Half Work at Sub-100 Companies; 62% Influence Tech Purchases
Company size distribution shows that 47% of developers work at organizations with fewer than 100 employees. Breaking this down: 18.5% at 2-9 person companies, 14.2% at 10-19, and 14.3% at 20-99. The remaining 53% are at larger organizations: 16.4% at 100-499 and 36.6% at 500+. More importantly, 62% of developers influence technology purchasing decisions at their organizations. The typical evaluation journey starts with a free trial (75% of respondents), followed by asking other developers for recommendations (73%). And 60% prefer a build-and-buy approach — using open-source or internal tools first, then purchasing commercial solutions when scaling. For product and go-to-market teams, this means developer experience is not just an engineering concern — it's a core go-to-market strategy.

## Slide 8: Strategic Takeaways
To summarize our five key findings. First, hybrid-first is the new default — 42% hybrid, 38% remote. Design your talent strategy and office footprint accordingly. Second, niche skills command significant premiums — Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir developers earn 50% more than mainstream stack developers. Third, U.S. full-time employment is softening, dropping from 69% to 64.8%, while freelancing remains durable at 16.4%. Fourth, developers are enterprise buyers — 62% influence purchases, and 75% start with free trials. Developer experience is a go-to-market strategy. Finally, compensation growth flattens after 15 years, so retention of senior talent requires more than salary — think scope, autonomy, and equity. Thank you.
